rows: One output for each allowed input; range: all attained outputs. Check denominators $\ne0$, real square-root arguments $\ge0$, logarithm arguments $>0$.
$(f\circ g)(x)=f(g(x))$. Require $x\in D_g$ and $g(x)\in D_f$. Order matters.
$f(x)\to L$ as $x\to a$: nearby nonzero offsets make outputs as close to $L$ as required. The value at $a$ need not exist or equal $L$.
At an interior point, a finite two-sided limit exists exactly when both one-sided limits exist and agree. At an interval endpoint, use the approach within the domain.
At an interior point: $f(a)$ exists, the finite two-sided limit exists, and $$\lim_{x\to a}f(x)=f(a).$$ At included endpoints use the inward one-sided limit. Check each join separately.
If $f(x)\to A$ and $g(x)\to B$: $$f\pm g\to A\pm B,\quad cf\to cA,\quad fg\to AB,\quad \frac{f}{g}\to\frac{A}{B}\ (B\ne0).$$ All component limits use the same approach and a common nearby domain.
If $g(x)\to L$ and $f$ is continuous at $L$: $$f(g(x))\to f(L).$$ Nearby inner outputs must lie in the outer domain.
Polynomials: continuous everywhere. Rational functions: denominator nonzero. $\sqrt{x}$: $x\ge0$; $\ln x$: $x>0$. Absolute value, sine, cosine and exponential: continuous on their real domains.
Equal rules on a deleted neighbourhood have the same limit. Cancellation preserves exclusions; a continuous extension is a separate definition.
Try valid substitution first. For $0/0$: factor, expand, combine fractions or multiply by a nonzero conjugate. $$ (A-B)(A+B)=A^2-B^2. $$ $0/0$ is an indeterminate form, not an answer.
$$|u|=\begin{cases}u,&u\ge0,\\-u,&u<0.\end{cases}$$ Split at a sign change before cancelling.

Unequal one-sided limits, unbounded growth or persistent oscillation can prevent a finite limit. A finite table or plot is evidence, not proof. Rounded subtraction of nearly equal numbers can lose accuracy.
$$\frac{\sqrt{9+h}-3}{h}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{9+h}+3}\to\frac16\quad(h\to0).$$ Equality on the original domain: $h\ge-9$, $h\ne0$. A finite-offset difference from $1/6$ is not necessarily rounding error.
